findings.title: The kiosk staff lookup reveals staff names and masked emails by guessable number, and sends setup emails without a dedicated rate limit.
findings.scenario: Anyone standing at the paired counter tablet in Tom's pharmacy can type 1, 2, 3 and so on into the Staff ID box. For Omar, Ali, Mia, and also Nadia at Tom's other pharmacy, the kiosk shows the full name, account number and a partly hidden email. Unknown numbers get a different 'not found' answer, so every staff member in the group can be listed. Anyone who has no PIN yet (for example a new starter like Jack) gets a setup-code email on every probe. The PIN clock screen deliberately gives one generic error so this cannot happen, but the lookup screen undoes that.
findings.test_needed: Using one device token, look up a known staff ID and an unknown one and assert both answers look the same with no name or email; then assert repeated lookups are rate-limited like the PIN screen.

owner_question.question: Someone at Tom's counter tablet types Staff ID numbers one after another. What should the kiosk show them?
options: Nothing that names anyone: the same neutral 'enter your PIN or check your email' answer for every number, rate-limited
Show names only for staff of this pharmacy, never staff from Tom's other pharmacies, and rate-limit lookups
Keep today's behaviour: show the name and partly hidden email so staff can confirm it is them

findings.title: The kiosk login check also accepts the stored token text as-is, so the scrambled copy saved in the database works as a kiosk token.
findings.scenario: Kiosk tokens are saved only in scrambled (hashed) form so that a leaked database or backup can't be used to sign in a kiosk. But the login check also accepts a token that matches the saved text exactly. So anyone who sees the saved value for Tom's front-counter kiosk (in a backup, an admin screen or a support export) can send it as the token and act as that kiosk: show sign-in QR codes, look up staff and clock people in. Nothing hashes old plain-text tokens, so this extra check is permanent.
findings.test_needed: Activate a kiosk, read its saved hash from the database, call authenticate_kiosk_device with that hash and assert it returns None.

owner_question.question: If someone gets a copy of Tom's database backup, should the kiosk token values in it be enough to run Tom's counter kiosk?
options: No: hash the old plain-text tokens once and accept only real tokens from then on
No: make old unhashed kiosks pair again, then drop the extra check
Keep today's behaviour so very old kiosks keep working
